claim: FamiSafe is a dual-app ecosystem: parent controller (com.wondershare.famisafe, 415-line manifest: 129 activities, 21 services, 14 receivers, 8 providers, 37 permissions) plus child enforcement agent (com.wondershare.famisafe.kids, 408-line manifest). Zero DeviceAdmin/Accessibility/VpnService in the parent package.
observed_fact: Parsed both AndroidManifest.xml files in full: parent declares 129 activities / 21 services / 14 receivers / 8 providers and 37 permissions with no enforcement components; child declares SCAccessibilityService, DeviceAdmin receiver, MainService, WatchDogService and 5 block UI activities. Proves dual-app topology, not PASA.

claim: ScreenTimeTool encodes weekly schedules as 7 comma-joined day elements; '-1'=no limit, '86400'=full day, other numbers are seconds; empty list defaults to the hardcoded literal '3600,-1,200,300,300,300,300'; HasInvalidSameSchedule is dead code with zero callers.
observed_fact: Read ScreenTimeTool.java fully (160 lines): getLimitString/getScheduleString produce 7-element comma strings; literal '3600,-1,200,300,300,300,300' returned verbatim at L106 for empty lists; HasInvalidSameSchedule at L26 has zero callers across all smali (verified by whole-tree search).

claim: Rules flow parent->cloud->child with no direct parent-child channel: parent POSTs form-urlencoded rules, child pulls the full ControlsBean via GET v4/gather/controls-init, stores it as JSON in SharedPreferences file 'controls_init_v5' key 'key_controls_init', and hot-reloads via EventBus.
observed_fact: MainService writes the full ControlsBean JSON into SharedPreferences file 'controls_init_v5' after requestControlsInit; MMKVChangeEvent('key_controls_init') triggers hot rule reload plus ruleChangeTriggerEventNow(). No socket or network IPC between parent and child packages exists anywhere in either tree.

claim: Parent rule contract: DeviceRuleBean is a Kotlin data class with snake_case fields and no @SerializedName (Gson field-name serialization), containing apps, block_device, schedule and screen_time; it is a read-model only with no writers in Java/smali.
observed_fact: DeviceRuleBean.java read in full: fields apps: List<App1>, block_app_icons, block_device, platform, schedule: List<List<String>>, screen_time: ScreenTime1, vpn_apps. Whole-tree search confirms zero writers — read-model only.

claim: Request signing uses MD5(APP_KEY + sorted params JSON + APP_FP) with both secrets hardcoded in ApiConstant.java; hosts are data-api.famisafe.com (overridable via ApiUrl.update()), app-api-pro.famisafe.com.
observed_fact: ApiConstant.java L6: APP_KEY = 'EE12071A4BC85EE516C78C38E78D1F14' hardcoded; signing formula vc = MD5(key + sorted-params + fp) reconstructed from call sites. Hardcoded secrets are explicitly rejected for Family OS reuse.

claim: Device pairing uses a match-code flow: parent requests GET v4/match-code/get and displays code + QR; child logs in with POST v5/member/match-code-login; parent polls GET v4/match-code/device-get for link discovery.
observed_fact: PairCodeActivity.smali contains requestPairCode() issuing GET v4/match-code/get and rendering PairCodeBean{match_code, install_url}; polling of device-get plus ActionMessageEvent listener confirmed in smali.

claim: Parent notifications are server-stored and pulled periodically (not pushed): GET v5/notification/list-get with cursor pagination; NotifyTool.getType classifies into dashboard card types (youtube_alert, screen_time, geo_fence, ...).
observed_fact: NotifyTool.getType maps model strings to card types; NotifyDetailBean{day_marking, filter, list, next_start_primary_key} shows cursor pagination. ParentNotifyService read fully: pure keep-alive foreground service, not a notification transport.

claim: Entitlement gate SpLoacalData.isVip() = (member_level == 1) OR future empower_expire; SKUs famisafe_monthly/quarterly/annual_subscription; server codes 492/509/513 disable the account locally.
observed_fact: BillingConstants.java declares SKU_GOLD_MONTHLY = 'famisafe_monthly_subscription' at L12 plus _uac_/_kids_/_first_coupon/lifetime/price_test variants; Google Play Billing 9.1.0 client; server verification POST v{1,5}/payment/notify.

claim: Child accessibility entry SCAccessibilityService (180 lines) is a pure dispatcher: ignores its own keyboard events and forwards the rest to AccessibilityManager when getCurrentUserRole() == 4 (child role); config uses typeAllMask + feedbackAllMask with canTakeScreenshot=true.
observed_fact: SCAccessibilityService.java read fully (180 lines): dispatcher only. accessibility_service_config.xml verified: typeAllMask, feedbackAllMask, notificationTimeout=100, canRetrieveWindowContent=true, canTakeScreenshot=true.

claim: Blocking is overlay-based with a never-kill policy: AppBlockStrategy evaluates ScreenBlockHelper <- ScheduleBlockHelper <- AppBlockHelper per window event and shows a fullscreen TYPE_APPLICATION_OVERLAY layer swallowing BACK; whole-tree search confirms zero killBackgroundProcesses/forceStopPackage/Process.killProcess in all child sources.
observed_fact: AppBlockStrategy read: three-helper priority evaluation, InterceptionAppPopupWindow then InterceptionAppActivity fallback. Exhaustive grep over the entire child tree returns zero hits for killBackgroundProcesses, forceStopPackage or Process.killProcess — blocked apps keep running under the overlay.

claim: Anti-tamper battery: AppDefenceUtils (374 lines) tries 9 defences per event (throttled 1/60s) including OEM launcher uninstall-dialog interception, 8-language date-settings detection, and AdminDefence (33 lines) catching device-admin deactivation; response g() (L127) sends BACK+HOME, shows warning, then DevicePolicyManager.lockNow().
observed_fact: AppDefenceUtils.java read fully (374 lines): LauncherHw/Mi/LongClick defences, DateSetDefence in 8 languages, MiAppInfoDefence, AppInfoDefence, GooglePermissionController, AccessibilityDefence, AdminDefence (33 lines, matches com.android.settings:id/admin_warning). g() at L127 performs lockNow(). No safe-mode handling, no password gate.

claim: DeviceAdmin receiver is a near-empty stub declaring only the force-lock policy; onDisableRequested returns super (null). Uninstall prevention comes from the OS (admin must be deactivated first) + accessibility interception of the deactivation dialog + lockNow() response.
observed_fact: DeviceAdmin.java: all callbacks log-and-super only; onDisableRequested at L30 returns super.onDisableRequested (null, no warning text). device_admin.xml declares <force-lock/> only. Activation via AdminActivePermission standard ACTION_ADD_DEVICE_ADMIN intent.

claim: ~38 social content scrapers (Instagram80Monitor, WhatsApp80Monitor, Telegram80Monitor, ...) scrape message text from accessibility nodes ('80' = Android 8.0+ node-parsing variants); BrowserMonitor maps per-browser URL-bar view IDs (Chrome url_bar at L84) and matches any package containing 'browser'.
observed_fact: BrowserMonitor.java L84: put('com.android.chrome', 'com.android.chrome:id/url_bar'); per-browser view-ID map plus substring 'browser' package matching confirmed. ~38 *80Monitor classes counted by filename pattern (PARTIAL-EVIDENCE on exact count: 38).

claim: Web filtering executes on-device but the verdict is server-side: blocking GET v1/gather/web-filter-check (10s timeout), cache 60s block / 300s allow, cleared on web_filter_update push; no local blocklist exists in child code.
observed_fact: BlockHandler performs blocking web-filter-check call with 10s timeout; block=60s / allow=300s cache policy read in code; no blocklist arrays or files found anywhere in child sources (absence verified by search).

claim: Command plane: FCM plus a persistent WebSocket (token from GET v5/member/ws-token) feed PushManager with id-based dedup (last 50); ChildPushListener handles ~30 actions directly (screen_limit, web_filter_update, screenshot, recorder_start/stop...), remainder goes to EventBus.
observed_fact: FirebaseMessageReceiver.java enumerates the action vocabulary (gather_now, controls_init_update, screen_limit, ...); WebSocketHelper.java is 250 lines. Commands carry no signature (security gap noted for Family OS).

claim: On-device geofence is custom math, not the Google Geofencing API: CustomGeoFence reads fences from ControlsBean.gps_fence, ComputeDistance.computeDistanceBetween (L19, haversine) measures distance, 5-minute dedup, then POST v1/gather/geo-fence-log.
observed_fact: ComputeDistance.java L19: public static double computeDistanceBetween (haversine via Math.asin/sqrt). CustomGeoFence consumes ControlsBean.gps_fence. Zero references to Google Geofencing API in the child tree.

claim: Keep-alive package: persistent MainService, WatchDogService in :watch process, mutual-restart DaemonProcess (126 lines), WakeUp receivers, evernote android-job, OEM boot lists (MIUI/Huawei; no Oppo/Vivo).
observed_fact: DaemonProcess.java is 126 lines implementing mutual restart between processes. MIUIStartPermission/HwPermission present; whole-tree search confirms no Oppo/Vivo helpers.

claim: Security anti-patterns (explicitly rejected for Family OS): empty checkServerTrusted in SSLSocketClient (trust-all TLS), usesCleartextTraffic=true in parent manifest (L56), hardcoded APP_KEY/APP_FP signing secrets, leaked Google Maps key in manifest.
observed_fact: SSLSocketClient.java L40-41: checkServerTrusted body is empty (trust-all). Parent manifest L56: usesCleartextTraffic='true'. All four items catalogued as do-not-reuse.
